newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kinkel meets Russians, no progress on NATO.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel meets Russians, no progress on NATO.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel met Russia's prime minister and defence minister on Wednesday but there was no sign of progress in the dispute over NATO's eastward expansion plans.
"Everyone I have met (in Moscow) has shown resistance to NATO enlargement," Kinkel said after the talks with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Defence Minister Igor Rodionov.

Russia opposes the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation's plans to take in former Soviet-bloc countries former eastern and central Europe, saying such moves would threaten its security and create divisions in Europe.
Kinkel arrived in Moscow on Tuesday ahead of visits this week by Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.

They want to ease Russian concerns over NATO's enlargement, with the aim of reaching agreement before an alliance summit in Madrid in July which is expected to issue membership invitations to Poland, Hungary and the Czech republic.
"We have to find a solution which allows us to have a successful summit in Madrid for all of us," Kinkel said, making clear he hoped Russia's concerns would be addressed.
He said he had sought to reassure Chernomyrdin and Rodionov that NATO enlargement was not aimed against Moscow and that the West wanted to build European security jointly with Russia.
Kinkel also had talks on Tuesday evening with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and Anatoly Chubais, President Boris Yeltsin's chief-of-staff in the Kremlin.
Primakov told a joint news conference after his two-hour meeting with Kinkel that Russia would always have a negative attitude towards NATO enlargement.
